business_model.basis: Stated directly in the 10-K Business section and 10-Q MD&A.
business_model.claim: Slide Insurance Holdings, Inc. underwrites single family, condominium, and commercial residential property and casualty insurance policies in coastal states along the Atlantic seaboard through Slide Insurance Company (licensed in Florida and South Carolina) and Slide Specialty Insurance Company (licensed in New Hampshire, New Jersey, New York, Rhode Island, and South Carolina).
quotes: We focus on profitable underwriting of single family, condominium and commercial residential policies in the property and casualty (P&C) industry in coastal states along the Atlantic seaboard through our insurance subsidiary, Slide Insurance Company (“SIC”).
SIC is licensed in Florida and South Carolina.

In February 2025, we acquired an additional insurance subsidiary, Slide Specialty Insurance Company ("Slide Specialty"), which is licensed in New Hampshire, New Jersey, New York, Rhode Island and South Carolina.

business_model.basis: Stated by CEO Bruce Lucas in the October 27, 2026 earnings release (Exhibit 99.1 to Form 8-K).
business_model.claim: Outside its Atlantic seaboard markets, Slide writes residential excess and surplus (E&S) policies in California and started writing residential business in Texas.
quotes: We achieved another quarter of double-digit growth on our bottom line while making solid progress with writing residential E&S policies in California and expanding our homeowners solutions in South Carolina and Rhode Island.
Earlier this month, we started writing residential business in Texas, further expanding our geographic footprint.

business_model.basis: Stated directly in the 10-K MD&A Overview.
business_model.claim: Slide reports its operations as a single reportable segment.
quotes: We have one reportable segment.

business_model.basis: Stated directly in the 10-K Business and Risk Factors sections and 10-Q MD&A.
business_model.claim: Slide acquires policies through inorganic block acquisitions—principally policy assumptions from Florida's Citizens Property Insurance Corporation and acquired renewal rights—and subsequent renewals, alongside new policies sold via independent agents and a direct-to-consumer (DTC) channel.
quotes: We acquire policies both from inorganic block acquisitions and subsequent renewals, as well as new business sales through a combination of independent agents and our direct-to-consumer (“DTC”) channel, through which we sell our insurance products directly to end consumers, without the use of retailers, brokers, agents or other intermediaries.

In addition, a substantial portion of our historical revenue has been generated from policies assumed from Citizens Property Insurance Corporation (“Citizens”), created by the Florida legislature in 2002 as not-for-profit, tax-exempt, government entity to provide property insurance to eligible Florida property owners unable to find insurance coverage in the private market, as well as our acquisition of policies from several Florida insurance companies and subsequent renewals of these policies.

business_model.basis: Stated directly in the 10-K and 10-Q MD&A.
business_model.claim: Underwriting revenue is driven by gross premiums written—moved by Citizens assumptions, third-party block acquisitions, renewals, new policy bindings, average premiums, and premium rates—which are earned ratably over 12 months for new and renewal policies or over the remaining term for Citizens assumptions.
quotes: Gross premiums written represent, with respect to a fiscal period, the sum of assumed premiums written from Citizens policy assumptions (net of opt-outs) plus direct premiums written (premiums from subsequent renewals of such Citizens policies and new and renewal policies written through independent agents and our DTC channel, net of any midterm cancellations), in each case prior to amounts ceded to reinsurers.

Gross premiums written associated with assumed policies from Citizens are earned ratably over the remaining term of the policy and gross premiums written associated with voluntary and renewal policies are earned ratably over the term of the policy.
All such new and renewal policies currently have a term of 12 months from date of issuance.

business_model.basis: Stated directly in the 10-K and 10-Q MD&A.
business_model.claim: Top-line growth has been propelled by Citizens assumptions (191,850 policies and $373 million in assumed unearned premiums in 2025; 47,718 policies and $102.5 million in 2026) and policy renewals, increasing policies in force from 343,056 at year-end 2024 to 493,532 at year-end 2025 even as average residential premium declined from $3,924 to $3,670.
quotes: In 2025 we assumed 191,850 policies, representing approximately $373 million in assumed unearned premiums from Citizens.
In 2026 we assumed 47,718 policies, representing approximately $102.5 million in assumed unearned premiums from Citizens.
Our policies in force as of December 31, 2025 and December 31, 2024 were approximately 493,532 and 343,056 respectively, and this increase had a favorable impact on our gross premiums earned.
Our average premium per residential policy decreased from $3,924 at December 31, 2024 to $3,670 at December 31, 2025 as a result of a decrease in average premium of Citizens policies assumed.

business_model.basis: Stated directly in the 10-K Business and MD&A and 10-Q MD&A.
business_model.claim: Reinsurance is Slide's single largest cost and reduces gross premiums earned to net premiums earned; ceded premiums earned rose from $304.9 million (27.8% of gross premiums earned) in 2024 to $411.7 million (27.6%) in 2025 as policy exposures grew.
quotes: Reinsurance is an important part of our risk management strategy and premiums paid to reinsurers is our single largest cost.
Ceded premiums for the year ended December 31, 2025 and 2024 were approximately $411.7 million and $304.9 million, respectively, representing 27.6% and 27.8%, respectively, of gross premiums earned.
The rates we pay for reinsurance are based primarily on policy exposures reflected in gross premiums earned.

business_model.basis: Stated directly in the 10-K and 10-Q MD&A.
business_model.claim: Slide generates net investment income by investing premium float ahead of claim payments—with average investable assets expanding from $986.3 million in 2024 to $1,763.7 million in 2025—driven by investment portfolio size and portfolio yield.
quotes: Because the payment of claims occurs after the receipt of the premium, often years later, we invest the cash in various investment securities that generally earn interest and dividends.
Factors affecting net investment income include the size of our investment portfolio and the yield generated by the underlying investments in our investment portfolio.
Our average investable assets increased to $1,763.7 million for the year ended December 31, 2025 from $986.3 million for the year ended December 31, 2024.

business_model.claim: Slide earns non-premium fee revenue from a non-refundable $25 upfront policy fee per policy written under Florida law, installment pay-plan fees, and retail agency commissions on policies sold for non-affiliated insurers.
quotes: Florida law allows insurers to charge policyholders a $25 policy fee on each policy written.

These fees are not subject to refund, and accordingly we recognize policy fees as income immediately when collected in accordance with ASC 606, which coincides with the completion of our service obligation when the policy is issued.
Other income represents all pay-plan fees and commission income earned by our retail agency subsidiary that sells on behalf of non-affiliated carriers.

business_model.basis: Stated directly in the 10-K MD&A, 10-Q MD&A, and Q3 2026 earnings release.
business_model.claim: Losses and loss adjustment expenses incurred, net depend on claim frequency and severity, catastrophe weather events, reinsurance recoveries, business mix, legal and regulatory conditions, and claims cost inflation, causing the loss ratio to move from 42.8% in 2024 to 21.8% in 2025 and 30.4% in the third quarter of 2026.
quotes: Losses and loss adjustment expenses incurred, net reflect losses paid, expenses paid to resolve claims, such as fees paid to adjusters, attorneys and investigators, and changes in our reserves for unpaid losses and loss adjustment expenses incurred, net during the fiscal period, in each case net of losses ceded to reinsurers.

Our loss ratio decreased to 21.8% for the year ended December 31, 2025 from 42.8% for the year ended December 31, 2024, primarily as a result of increased net premiums earned from increased policies in force and a decrease in catastrophe losses from hurricane and non-hurricane weather activity.
This resulted in a loss ratio of 30.4%, compared to 13.7% in the prior-year period.

business_model.basis: Stated directly in the 10-K and 10-Q MD&A.
business_model.claim: Policy acquisition and other underwriting expenses—comprising outside agent commissions, premium taxes, and inspection fees—are amortized over the policy term and rose from 10.8% of net premiums earned in 2024 to 12.9% in 2025 because newly assumed Citizens policies incur no upfront acquisition costs until renewal.
quotes: Policy acquisition and other underwriting expenses consist of the following items: (i) commissions paid to outside agents at the time of policy issuance, (ii) premium taxes and (iii) inspection fees.
We recognize policy acquisition and other underwriting expenses ratably over the term of the underlying policy.
Until renewed, policies assumed from Citizens have no associated policy acquisition and other underwriting expenses.

Policy acquisition and other underwriting expenses for the year ended December 31, 2025 and 2024 were approximately $139.4 million and $86.0 million, respectively, representing 12.9% and 10.8% of net premiums earned, respectively.

business_model.basis: Stated directly in the 10-K and 10-Q MD&A.
business_model.claim: General and administrative expenses—comprising compensation and benefits, professional fees, office leases, information systems, and corporate insurance—rose to $175.8 million in 2025 as personnel grew from 346 to 504, though premium growth lowered the G&A share of net premiums earned from 17.4% to 16.3%.
quotes: General and administrative expenses include compensation and related benefits, professional fees, office lease and related expenses, information system expenses, corporate insurance, and other general and administrative costs.

General and administrative expenses for the year ended December 31, 2025 and 2024 and were approximately $175.8 million and $137.5 million , respectively, representing 16.3% and 17.4%, respectively, of net premiums earned.
Personnel count increased to 504 at December 31, 2025 from 346 at December 31, 2024.

business_model.basis: Stated directly in the 10-K Business section.
business_model.claim: Slide's vertically integrated operating model relies on its proprietary $8.9 trillion TIV dataset, underwriting automation, and owned claims and mitigation capabilities to price individual policy profitability and forward-looking reinsurance costs at the point of sale.
quotes: We control all aspects of our value chain, including technology, underwriting, actuarial, distribution, claims, risk management and reinsurance which allows us to maximize profitability while maintaining disciplined underwriting standards.

Our underwriting technology has been an important component of our success and is backed by our proprietary approximately $8.9 trillion TIV underwriting and claims dataset, which provides us with real-time intelligence to drive superior decision making.

Our model estimates forward-looking reinsurance costs on a policy level basis and dynamically adjusts the reinsurance cost as the amount at risk, concentration and other factors change across the portfolio, enabling us to accurately predict reinsurance costs at the policy level.

business_model.basis: Stated directly in the 10-K and 10-Q MD&A.
business_model.claim: Underwriting profitability is measured by the combined ratio (52.1% in 2025 and 59.3% in the third quarter ended September 30, 2026), while non-underwriting costs consist of interest expense, depreciation of property and internal-use software, amortization of renewal rights and intangibles, and corporate income taxes.
quotes: Combined ratio is the sum of the loss ratio and the expense ratio.
A combined ratio under 100% indicates an underwriting profit.
Depreciation expense includes depreciation of property and equipment, including software developed for internal use.
Amortization expense includes amortization of renewal rights and other intangible assets.

competitive_position.basis: stated in the cited items (P1 and P4 business overview)
competitive_position.claim: Slide operates as a coastal specialty property and casualty insurer targeting underserved single family, condominium, and commercial residential markets where national carriers have pulled back, such as Florida where large national carriers' share of premium fell from 62% in 1999 to 28% in 2022.
quotes: We focus on profitable underwriting of single family, condominium and commercial residential policies in the property and casualty (P&C) industry in coastal states along the Atlantic seaboard through our insurance subsidiary, Slide Insurance Company (“SIC”).

A prime example of this market shift is Florida, where large national carriers have reduced their market share of premium from 62% in 1999 to 28% in 2022, creating an opportunity for accretive expansion.

Coastal specialty market demand for insurance products has increased over the last few years as the larger, national insurance carriers have reduced their underwriting capacity in such markets, creating a unique market opportunity for us to capitalize on the imbalance of supply and demand.

competitive_position.basis: stated in the cited items (P4 subsidiary overview and P6 Q3 2026 earnings release dated October 27, 2026)
competitive_position.claim: Slide has expanded its geographic footprint beyond Florida and South Carolina through Slide Specialty Insurance Company's licenses in New Hampshire, New Jersey, New York, Rhode Island, and South Carolina, alongside 2026 launches in California residential E&S and Texas residential business.
quotes: SIC is licensed in Florida and South Carolina.

In February 2025, we acquired an additional insurance subsidiary, Slide Specialty Insurance Company ("Slide Specialty"), which is licensed in New Hampshire, New Jersey, New York, Rhode Island and South Carolina.

We achieved another quarter of double-digit growth on our bottom line while making solid progress with writing residential E&S policies in California and expanding our homeowners solutions in South Carolina and Rhode Island.
Earlier this month, we started writing residential business in Texas, further expanding our geographic footprint.

competitive_position.basis: stated in the cited item (P1 business and distribution sections)
competitive_position.claim: Slide controls its end-to-end insurance value chain and pairs inorganic block acquisitions with independent agents using its proprietary Violet quoting system and a direct-to-consumer channel.
quotes: We control all aspects of our value chain, including technology, underwriting, actuarial, distribution, claims, risk management and reinsurance which allows us to maximize profitability while maintaining disciplined underwriting standards.

We acquire policies both from inorganic block acquisitions and subsequent renewals, as well as new business sales through a combination of independent agents and our direct- to-consumer (“DTC”) channel, through which we sell our insurance products directly to end consumers, without the use of retailers, brokers, agents or other intermediaries.
Violet, our proprietary underwriting system, allows our agents to quickly bind a policy within minutes, which we believe helps to drive improved quote and bind ratios.

competitive_position.basis: stated in the cited item (P1 underwriting, claims, and technology sections)
competitive_position.claim: Slide supports underwriting and claims differentiation with an approximately $8.9 trillion TIV dataset, AI-filtered aerial imagery, in-house attritional claims handling, and post-catastrophe roof damage scoring within 48 hours of an event.
quotes: Our underwriting technology has been an important component of our success and is backed by our proprietary approximately $8.9 trillion TIV underwriting and claims dataset, which provides us with real-time intelligence to drive superior decision making.

We use post-catastrophe aerial imagery and roof damage scores for all affected risks within 48 hours of an event along with our traditional overlaid storm track information, to triage our catastrophe response and deploy our construction resources to mitigate the damage.

We aim to handle all claims with our employees, and do not intend to outsource our attritional claims functions at any point apart from field adjusting or inspection services, where we may use outside personnel.

competitive_position.basis: stated in the cited items (P1 business overview and P3 MD&A)
competitive_position.claim: Financial results from 2021 through 2025 demonstrate rapid scaling and underwriting profitability, as shareholders' equity grew from $102 million to $1,113 million (55% CAGR), in-force premium reached $1,796 million, and Slide averaged a 66.3% combined ratio, posting a 52.1% combined ratio and 57.4% return on equity in 2025.
quotes: We have grown our shareholders’ equity from $102 million at the end of 2021 to $1,113 million at the end of 2025, a CAGR of 55%.
In this same time period, we have grown our in force premium to $1,796 million at the end of 2025, while running an average consolidated combined ratio of 66.3%.
Our return on equity and combined ratio were 57.4% and 52.1% for 2025, and 60.0% and 72.3% for 2024, respectively.

competitive_position.claim: Profitable growth continued in the third quarter of 2026, with gross premiums written rising 9.3% year-over-year to $506.6 million, net income rising 24.5% to $138.2 million, and a 59.3% combined ratio compared to 48.5% in the prior-year period.
quotes: Gross premiums written grew 9.3% to $506.6 million, compared to $463.4 million in the prior-year period.
Net income grew 24.5% to $138.2 million, compared to $111.0 million in the prior-year period.

Combined ratio of 59.3%, compared to 48.5% in the prior-year period, primarily reflecting higher catastrophe losses during the quarter as compared to the prior year period, partially offset by improved operating leverage.

Total shareholders' equity | 1,302,663 | 1,113,241

competitive_position.basis: stated in the cited item (P2 Risk Factors, incorporated unchanged by P5)
competitive_position.claim: While SIC and SSIC hold an A, Exceptional Financial Stability Rating from Demotech, Slide lacks an AM Best rating, which may deter prospective customers, limit credit access, and constrain its ability to compete with large national and certain regional insurers.
quotes: SIC and SSIC currently have a Financial Stability Rating (“FSR”) of A, Exceptional from Demotech, Inc. (“Demotech”), a financial analysis firm that provides FSRs and consulting services for property and casualty insurance companies and title underwriters.
Furthermore, we do not currently have a rating from AM Best Company, a U.S.-based credit rating agency (“AM Best”).

It is possible that some prospective customers may be reluctant to do business with a company that is not rated by AM Best and not having an AM Best rating may prevent us from expanding our business or limit our access to credit from certain financial institutions, which may in turn limit our ability to compete with large, national insurance companies and certain regional insurance companies.

competitive_position.basis: stated in the cited item (P2 Risk Factors, incorporated unchanged by P5)
competitive_position.claim: A downgrade in Slide's financial strength ratings could weaken its marketplace competitiveness, impair policyholder attraction and retention, restrict capital and borrowing access, and trigger regulatory intervention.
quotes: A downgrade in our financial strength ratings, such as those provided by Demotech, Inc., could materially and adversely affect our business.

Such a downgrade may reduce our competitiveness in the marketplace, impair our ability to attract new customers or retain existing policyholders, limit the marketability of our insurance products, decrease sales volumes, and increase the cost or restrict our access to capital markets and other sources of liquidity, including borrowings.

competitive_position.basis: stated in the cited item (P2 Risk Factors, incorporated unchanged by P5)
competitive_position.claim: Slide faces intense competition in Florida, South Carolina, and expansion markets from established insurers that possess greater financial resources, higher financial ratings, stronger name recognition, broader capital access, larger agency networks, and bundled products.
quotes: The homeowners and commercial residential insurance markets, particularly in Florida and South Carolina where we currently operate as an admitted carrier, are highly competitive.

Some of our competitors have substantially greater financial resources, higher financial ratings, greater name recognition, broader access to capital, more extensive agency networks, and the ability to offer bundled products.

Increased competition could lead to pricing pressure, reduced premium adequacy, challenges in retaining existing business or underwriting new policies on favorable terms, shifts in supply and demand dynamics, or difficulties in maintaining relationships with customers, agents, and other third-party partners.

competitive_position.basis: stated in the cited item (P2 Risk Factors, incorporated unchanged by P5)
competitive_position.claim: Emerging technology-driven entrants and traditional insurers adopting comparable technologies could erode Slide's underwriting, distribution, and claims-processing technology advantages.
quotes: We also face emerging competition from technology-driven companies and entrants that have begun operating in adjacent insurance categories and may expand into homeowners and commercial residential products, potentially offering more competitive pricing, innovative distribution, or advanced claims processing capabilities that could erode any advantages we have developed through our technology platform.
Traditional insurers may similarly adapt by incorporating similar technologies, leveraging their greater scale and resources to further intensify competition.

competitive_position.basis: stated in the cited item (P2 Risk Factors, incorporated unchanged by P5)
competitive_position.claim: Having commenced operations in March 2021 and written its first policy in March 2022, Slide has a limited operating history and less brand recognition than incumbents, leaving its competitive position vulnerable to negative publicity or slower claims processing.
quotes: We began operations in March 2021 and wrote our first policy on March 1, 2022.
Many of our competitors have brands that are well recognized.

The speed by which we process and pay claims is a differentiating factor for our business and an increase in the average time to process claims could undermine our reputation and position in the insurance marketplace.

competitive_position.basis: stated in the cited items (P2 Risk Factors, P3 2025 10-K MD&A, and P4 Q3 2026 10-Q MD&A)
competitive_position.claim: A substantial share of Slide's historical revenue came from Citizens policy assumptions and acquisitions, exposing future growth if Citizens discontinues or curtails its depopulation program; assumed Citizens policies fell from 191,850 in 2025 to 47,718 in 2026.
quotes: In addition, a substantial portion of our historical revenue has been generated from policies assumed from Citizens Property Insurance Corporation (“Citizens”), created by the Florida legislature in 2002 as not-for-profit, tax-exempt, government entity to provide property insurance to eligible Florida property owners unable to find insurance coverage in the private market, as well as our acquisition of policies from several Florida insurance companies and subsequent renewals of these policies.
There can be no assurance that Citizens will decide to continue the depopulation program for a significant period of time, or at all.
In 2025 we assumed 191,850 policies, representing approximately $373 million in assumed unearned premiums from Citizens.
In 2026 we assumed 47,718 policies, representing approximately $102.5 million in assumed unearned premiums from Citizens.

competitive_position.basis: stated in the cited items (P1 Reinsurance and P2 Risk Factors)
competitive_position.claim: Reinsurance is Slide's single largest cost, and reduced availability or higher pricing upon treaty renewal, or reinsurer counterparty non-performance, could force Slide to retain more catastrophe risk, raise costs, or curtail underwriting volume.
quotes: Reinsurance is an important part of our risk management strategy and premiums paid to reinsurers is our single largest cost.

We may be unable to renew or replace expiring treaties on comparable terms, limits, or pricing, or at all, which could force us to retain more risk, reduce underwriting volume, or incur higher reinsurance costs that pressure profitability until premium rates can be adjusted, subject to regulatory approval.
Reinsurance does not relieve us of our primary liability to policyholders for covered losses, and we remain obligated to pay claims even if our reinsurers fail to perform.

competitive_position.basis: stated in the cited item (P2 Risk Factors, incorporated unchanged by P5)
competitive_position.claim: State insurance regulations can delay rate adjustments, restrict policy non-renewals or cancellations, and delay or block regulatory approvals needed to expand into new states or product verticals.
quotes: State insurance regulations may further limit our ability to non-renew policies, cancel coverage, or implement timely rate increases in response to adverse loss experience or changing conditions, potentially requiring us to retain unprofitable business or incur higher reinsurance or other costs.
In addition to the need for substantial resources, insurance regulation could limit our ability to introduce new product offerings.

Moreover, as we introduce new insurance products or lines of business beyond our current homeowners and commercial residential focus, we expect to encounter competition from carriers with established positions in those areas, and any such new products may require months for regulatory approval or may not be approved at all.

competitive_position.basis: stated in the cited items (P2 Risk Factors and P6 Q3 2026 earnings release)
competitive_position.claim: Slide's profitability and capital remain exposed to pricing inaccuracies, potential loss reserve deficiencies, and catastrophe losses, including $34.2 million of third quarter 2026 Florida convective storm losses and up to $50 million of expected fourth quarter 2026 pre-tax losses from Hurricane Isaias.
quotes: Any material inaccuracies in our pricing methodology or inability to adjust rates effectively could result in adverse selection, increased loss ratios, reduced profitability, and a material adverse effect on our business, results of operations, and financial condition.

If any of our insurance reserves should prove to be inadequate for the reasons discussed above, or for any other reason, we would be required to increase reserves, which may negatively affect our net income and shareholders’ equity in the period in which the deficiency is identified.

Losses and loss adjustment expenses (LAE) incurred, net were $101.3 million, which included $34.2 million of catastrophe losses from convective storms in Florida in the quarter and $18.0 million of favorable prior period reserve development.
The Company’s updated range is inclusive of up to $50 million of pre-tax losses related to Hurricane Isaias in the fourth quarter.
